sensors.name: light sensor LLIGHT (the light from above)

control_flow: avoidWalls: if LLIGHT is below 70 %, check the sides: a wall on the left turns it left 20°, else a wall on the right turns it right 20°, else call driveInTheDark; if bright, call driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if LLIGHT is below 70 %, drive forward at 30 %; else call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: In the dark tunnel, don't hit its walls: turn away from a wall on its side and drive on through.

decision_points.condition: the left light sensor reads less than 70 % (it is in dim light, inside a tunnel)

branches.outcome: dim: it looks at its sides for walls
bright: it goes on to driveInTheDark

decision_points.condition: in the dark, first: an obstacle on the left; second: an obstacle on the right

branches.outcome: a wall in front of its left half: it turns left 20°
a wall in front of its right half: it turns right 20°
no wall on either side: it goes on to driveInTheDark

decision_points.condition: the left light sensor reads less than 70 %

branches.outcome: bright: it goes on to stopAtWall
nothing ahead: it goes on to followLine

scenarios.coded_response: In dim light, with no wall on its left or right, it drives forward at 30 %.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot stands inside a straight tunnel, in dim light, with nothing in front of it on either side.
scenarios.trigger: The program starts and keeps looping.
scenarios.title: Drives through a straight tunnel
assumptions: You didn't say where it should get to: the tunnel's far opening is taken as the place to reach.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It drives through the tunnel without touching its walls and gets out.

scenarios.coded_response: It turns left 20° at 30 % when the left sensor sees a wall, and right 20° when the right sensor sees one.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot is in dim light in a tunnel that bends, so a tunnel wall comes in front of its left half (or, in the other bend, its right half).
scenarios.trigger: The obstacle sensor on that side sees the wall.
scenarios.title: Turns away from a tunnel wall in the dark
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It turns away from the wall it sees and gets through the bend without touching the tunnel's walls.

scenarios.coded_response: It stops and stays stopped while the wall is ahead.
scenarios.initial_condition: In bright light, outside any tunnel, a wall in front of the robot, near enough to be seen at once.
scenarios.trigger: The front obstacle sensor sees the wall.
scenarios.title: Stops at a wall in bright light
assumptions: You said nothing about bright light; stopping at a wall ahead is taken as what the program means.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops before the wall without bumping into it.

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left on black and right on the floor.
scenarios.initial_condition: In bright light, outside any tunnel, on a black line, with nothing ahead.
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees black, then the floor, again and again.
scenarios.title: Follows the line in bright light
assumptions: You said nothing about the line; following it is taken as what the program means in bright light.

uncertainties: In the dark a wall on its left makes it turn left (into that wall) and a wall on its right makes it turn right, so its turning away may be the wrong way round.
In bright light it ignores walls on its sides completely: it only stops at a wall ahead, and otherwise follows the line.
In bright light it never drives straight: outside a tunnel a tunnel test has to start inside the tunnel where it is dim, or it turns away in a curve.
It decides whether it is dark from the left light sensor only.
